Owner Stephen M. Ross (team owner). $350M privately funded renovation 2015-16. Wikipedia infobox football capacity 64,767; 65,326 permanent seats. 193 executive suites (3,198 seats).
Owner and operator Kraft Group. Suite count differs by source (Wikipedia 82; other sources 89 or 92).

Owner NJ Sports & Exposition Authority; operator New Meadowlands Stadium Company LLC (Jets-Giants joint venture), so stadium revenue is shared 50/50 with the Giants. Wikipedia says 'approximately 218' suites. 2023-25 work was a turf replacement and FIFA lower-bowl renovations.

stadium.notes: Owner Maryland Stadium Authority; operator Ravens. Multi-year renovation finished in 2026 (Wikipedia $489M; the team has cited $430M). Premium counts come from a ticket-reseller summary (142 private suites plus 10 Blackwing suites; 8,332 club seats).
Owner Hamilton County; operator Bengals. In 2026 the lease was extended to 2036 and a multi-phase upgrade was announced (not yet completed).
Owner City of Cleveland; operator Browns. Renovated 2014-15. Club seat total not published.
Owner Sports & Exhibition Authority of Pittsburgh and Allegheny County; operators Steelers and Univ. of Pittsburgh. Renovated 2007, expanded 2015.

Wikipedia says the stadium is again named Reliant Stadium as of 2026. Owner Harris County Sports & Convention Corp.; operator ASM Global, so team revenue control is not stated. Club seats are listed as 'over 7,000' (a floor).

Owner Indiana Stadium and Convention Building Authority; operator Capital Improvement Board of Marion County. Football capacity 63,000, expandable to 70,000 (the NFL stadium list gives 67,000). Club seat total not stated.

Owner City of Jacksonville; operator ASM Global. A $1.4B 'Stadium of the Future' renovation runs 2025-2028: 2026 capacity is reduced to 42,507, the Jaguars play 2027 at Camping World Stadium (Orlando), and the rebuilt stadium (~63,000) reopens in 2028. Capacity and premium counts are pre-renovation. Wikipedia also cites '75 executive suites', which is ambiguous.
Owner and operator Metro Nashville. 2026 is the final season here; a new enclosed ~60,000-seat Nissan Stadium opens in 2027. 2012 was a mid-year upgrade, not a major renovation.

sources.teamControlsRevenue: https://www.empowerfieldatmilehigh.com/stadium/about-us (managed by Stadium Management Company LLC, a Broncos subsidiary)

stadium.notes: Owner Metropolitan Football Stadium District. Official site: 144 luxury suites and 8,200 club seats (Wikipedia says 132 suites). More than $100M in upgrades were completed in 2023.

Owner Jackson County Sports Complex Authority; operator Chiefs (lease 1972-2030). Named GEHA Field at Arrowhead 2021-2026. Major renovation 2007-10 ($375M); $50M FIFA work in 2025. Club seat total not stated.

Owner Las Vegas Stadium Authority; operator AEG Facilities. Capacity 65,000, expandable to 71,835. Wikipedia mentions '70+ significant ticketed events in 2025-26', which is too vague to record as nonLeagueEventsPerYear.

stadium.notes: Owner StadCo LA and Hollywood Park Land Co. (Kroenke, Rams owner); 'team' here means the Rams' owner, not the Chargers. The Chargers are a tenant, so false is an inference (est). Sources cite 'more than 13,000 premium seats'; the club-only total is unpublished.

sources.teamControlsRevenue: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SoFi_Stadium (operator StadCo LA, controlled by Rams owner Kroenke)

stadium.notes: Owner and operator StadCo LA (Kroenke). 'More than 13,000 premium seats' are cited (sofistadium.com/ALSD); the club-only total is unpublished.
Owner City of Arlington; operator Cowboys. Capacity 80,000, expandable past 100,000. A search summary says about 15,000 club seats (unverified, so left null).
Owner City of Philadelphia; operator Eagles. 172 suites (3,040 suite seats). Renovated 2013-14.
Owner Commanders; operator Harris Blitzer Sports & Entertainment. New RFK-site stadium planned for about 2030. Club seat total not stated.
Owner Chicago Park District; operator ASM Global. Rebuilt 2002-03. A search summary says 8,000 club seats (unverified, so left null).
Owner Detroit/Wayne County Stadium Authority; operator Lions. $100M renovation 2017.
Owner City of Green Bay; operator not stated. Renovated 2001-03, 2012-15, 2023. Packers site: 'approximately 3,000 outdoor and 3,000 indoor club seats'.
Owner Minnesota Sports Facilities Authority; operator ASM Global. Capacity 66,202, expandable to 73,000. Other sources say 135 or 141 suites; club counts vary (7,500-9,000), so left null.

sources.teamControlsRevenue: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercedes-Benz_Stadium (operator AMB Sports and Entertainment, Arthur Blank's company)

stadium.notes: Owner Georgia World Congress Center Authority (state); operator AMB Sports & Entertainment (team owner's company).

Owner and operator Tepper Sports & Entertainment. City of Charlotte is funding $650M of an $800M renovation (now $1.3B, 2026-2030) in exchange for the team staying through 2045. Club seat total not published.

sources.suites: https://www.caesarssuperdome.com/suites-at-caesars-superdome (value from web-search summary; page not directly verified)

stadium.notes: Owner Louisiana Stadium & Exposition District; operator Legends Global. Renovation of $450-560M in phases, finished by Super Bowl LIX (Feb 2025). Suites per search summary: 64 on 400 level, 89 on 300 level, 12 field level = 165.
Owner Hillsborough County; operator Tampa Sports Authority. Capacity 69,218, expandable to 75,000.
Owner Arizona Sports & Tourism Authority; operator Legends Global. 88 'luxury lofts'. Capacity 63,400, expandable to 72,200.

Owner Santa Clara Stadium Authority; operator Forty Niners Football Company LLC. The 7,500 club seats figure comes from the 2006 proposal. Wikipedia cites 'more than 200 private events annually' (not ticketed public events, so not recorded).
Owner Washington State Public Stadium Authority; operator First & Goal Inc. (Seahawks-affiliated operator). Club seats listed as 'over 7,000' (a floor).

sources.suites: https://suitehop.com/venues/td-garden-suites (value from web-search summary; page not directly verified)

stadium.notes: Owner and operator Delaware North (Jacobs family, which owns the NHL Bruins), not the Celtics. 'team' = owner of a co-tenant team; the Celtics are a tenant (inferred false). About 3.5M visitors a year.

Owner Empire State Development / Brooklyn Arena LDC; operator BSE Global (Nets' parent) with ASM Global. A $150M renovation (2024-26) converts 30 suites into clubs, so the older 101-suite count is stale and left null.

Owner MSG Entertainment, separate from Knicks owner MSG Sports though both are Dolan-controlled; the Knicks play under an arena license, so false is inferred. Transformation 2011-13. The events figure counts all events, including Knicks and Rangers games.
Owner Comcast Spectacor (Flyers owner); operator OVG360. 'team' = the Flyers' owner; the 76ers are a tenant. 1,880 'club-box' seats.
Owner and operator MLSE (Raptors' parent). Suite count varies by event ('up to 97' per a search summary), so left null.

Owner and operator United Center Joint Venture (Bulls 50% / Blackhawks 50%). Wikipedia: 169 executive suites after the 2009-10 renovation. For 2025-26 a new Banner Level replaced 74 Penthouse suites, so the current count may differ. Built with 3,000 club seats; current club total not stated.
Owner Gateway Economic Development Corp.; operator Dan Gilbert via Rocket Companies (Cavs owner). $185M transformation finished 2019.
Owner Downtown Development Authority; operator 313 Presents / Olympia Entertainment (Ilitch, Red Wings owner). The Pistons are a tenant (inferred false).

Owner and operator Capital Improvement Board of Marion County. $360M 'Fieldhouse of the Future' renovation 2020-22. Premium counts ambiguous (a search summary said '69 luxury suites and 2,400 club suites'), so left null.
Owner Atlanta Fulton County Recreation Authority; operator Hawks. 92 luxury suites + 9 party suites; 1,866 club seats.
Owner City of Charlotte; operator Hornets Sports & Entertainment. Arena page lists NBA capacity 19,444; the NBA arenas list says 19,077.
Owner Miami-Dade County; operator Basketball Properties Ltd. (Heat affiliate). Also 76 private boxes (per search summary).
Owner City of Orlando; operator Orlando Venues (city). Suites = 32 Founders + 28 Presidents; also 68 loge boxes and other premium areas (161 premium options in total).

Owner Monumental Sports & Entertainment (Wizards' parent). A ~$800M-1B transformation (DC contributing $515M) is underway through 2027; premium inventory is changing, so left null. yearRenovated = last completed renovation (2019-20).

Privately owned and operated by Kroenke Sports & Entertainment (Nuggets' owner). The official site gives basketball capacity 19,099; Wikipedia gives 19,520. A $135M renovation was announced Sept 2026.
Owner City of Minneapolis; operator Legends Global. Renovated 2017. The NBA arenas list gives 18,024.
Owner City of Oklahoma City; operator ASM Global. Renovated 2008-11. A new city-built arena is planned for about 2029-30.
Wikipedia: City of Portland bought the arena in 2024 ($7.13M from the Paul Allen estate); operator Rip City Management (Blazers). 70 suites plus 8 skyboxes. Renovation under negotiation.
Owner Ryan Smith (Jazz owner); operator Smith Entertainment Group. Renovated 2017 and 2024; a full dual-use renovation began April 2025, so premium counts may be changing.
Privately financed ($1.4B); the Warriors own and operate it. A search summary lists 44 Club Suites, 32 Courtside Suites and 60 Theater Boxes, but no clear suite total, so left null.
Owner Steve Ballmer (Murphy's Bowl LLC). NBA arenas list gives 18,000. Suite total not published in sources checked.
Owned and operated by AEG, not the Lakers ('team' = AEG, owner of the NHL Kings); the Lakers are a tenant (inferred false). 160 suites include 15 event suites. Renovated 2022-24.
Owner City of Phoenix; operator Phoenix Arena Development LP (Suns). $230M renovation completed 2020-21. Suites 'over 70' per a search summary, so left null.
Owner City of Sacramento; operator Sacramento Kings LP. Suites = 34 luxury + 48 loft-style suites.

Owner Louisiana Stadium & Exposition District; operator ASM Global.
